cavailles.oneLineEn: Philosophy of the concept and philosophy of mathematics; linked to Canguilhem and Foucault.

cd-broad.oneLineEn: Cambridge synthesizer in philosophy of mind, ethics, and metaphysics after Moore.

chen-que.oneLineEn: Ming-Qing Confucian who, in Disputing the Great Learning, challenged canonical Neo-Confucian reading.

cheng-xuanying.oneLineEn: Tang Daoist scholar known for Laozi-Zhuangzi subcommentaries and Chongxuan thought.

ci-lewis.oneLineEn: Conceptual pragmatism and modal logic; fills the Peirce-to-Quine American analytic line.

claude-lefort.oneLineEn: Empty place of democracy and critique of totalitarianism; after Castoriadis.

condillac.oneLineEn: Sensationalism that systematized Locke; the statue analogy is a key epistemology clue.

condorcet.oneLineEn: Progressive history and social mathematics linking Enlightenment politics to later positivism.

cornelius-castoriadis.oneLineEn: Social imaginary and autonomy theory; fills heterodox Western Marxism and political philosophy.

cournot.oneLineEn: Hub of probability, economics, and philosophy of science between Comte and later French epistemology.

cui-shu.oneLineEn: Qing evidential scholar who, in Records Examining Credibility, tested ancient historical transmission.

dalai-lama-14.oneLineEn: Contemporary Gelug leader bringing Madhyamaka, ethics, and science dialogue into global philosophy.

daosheng.oneLineEn: Eastern Jin–Liu Song monk known for sudden enlightenment and the icchantika-buddhahood debate.

david-armstrong.oneLineEn: Australian realist and physicalist in philosophy of mind; fills contemporary metaphysics.

dhammapala.oneLineEn: Theravāda Pali commentator linked to Paramatthadīpanī Khuddaka commentaries (ca. 6th–7th c., uncertain).

diderot.oneLineEn: Encyclopédie editor linking Enlightenment knowledge projects, materialism, and aesthetic criticism.

dolpopa.oneLineEn: Jonang systematizer whose other-emptiness (zhentong) marks a major Tibetan Madhyamaka divide.

duhem.oneLineEn: Holism and underdetermination (Duhem thesis); precursor of Quine.

eric-voegelin.oneLineEn: Political religion and philosophy of order; fills a conservative genealogy of modernity critique.
